scope: Focused offline payload research; no additional topology semantics claimed and no production decoder added.
observations: Both planar-trim bounded-face payloads contain 107 signed little-endian words (428 bytes). Their name tables contain nine and ten entries respectively.

Twelve aligned words differ between the trim payloads. Six differences swap values 0 and 2; looking up those candidate indices gives identical name terms across the two tables. Thus a raw word difference alone is not evidence of a changed trim-side field.

The other six changed word positions remain unresolved; one changes -1 to 9 and names 2, 7, 8 or 9 occur in the differing name tables. This is insufficient to define a cell-side bit or reconstruct selected boundary loops.

The tapped-hole input-face payload has prefix [0,-1,4], followed by four 29-word slices with shared marker positions in all three captured tapped-hole variants. The slices are not byte-identical. This is a structural repetition, not a verified count-to-edge or graph mapping.
The tapped-hole thread-face payload has prefix [0,-1,2] and 61 words (244 bytes), with a different remainder structure. A fixed 29-word record interpretation does not generalize.

The Boundary Fill face_recipe_data samples retain the simple [0,-1] payload even when their name-table entries have multiple terms. The geometric distinctions can be carried in the name terms rather than a changing payload.

trim_pair.warning: Candidate lookup is an analysis of aligned changed words only. It does not prove every nonnegative payload word is a name-table reference.

next_discriminating_capture: Capture a translated or rotated otherwise identical planar trim, then a second nonrectangular boundary and a trim using a second tool. Record pre-trim face/edge/vertex counts and both kept/removed cell bounds; test any proposed recursive grammar against all cases before assigning topology semantics.
limitations: No universal recursive payload grammar recovered.
No mapping from payload words to ASM face, edge or vertex indices established.
No topology rebuilding or native-file writing.
